title: On the Hyperparameter Loss Landscapes of Machine Learning Models: An Exploratory Study

problem.claim: The topography of machine-learning hyperparameter loss landscapes, which governs the HPO search process, is insufficiently understood.

gap.claim: Prior landscape analyses examined isolated landscapes and did not investigate structural similarities across scenarios; this exploration was missing.

contributions.claim: The paper maps 1,500 hyperparameter loss landscapes from 6 representative machine-learning models across 63 datasets and different fidelity levels, covering more than 11 million configurations.
The paper analyzes the mapped landscapes using fine-grained visualizations and dedicated fitness-landscape-analysis metrics.
Artifacts associated with the paper are made available through the cited GraphFLA repository.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report observing similar landscape topography across a wide range of models, datasets, and fidelities.
The authors report that the analysis sheds light on the mechanism behind the success of several popular HPO methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing HPO work emphasizes algorithmic advances while the governing hyperparameter loss landscapes remain poorly understood.
Existing fitness-landscape analyses do not examine structural similarities among landscapes induced in different scenarios.
The study maps 1,500 landscapes spanning 6 models, 63 datasets, multiple fidelity levels, and more than 11 million configurations.
Exploratory analysis reports similar topography across models, datasets, and fidelities and links it to the success of several HPO methods.
Associated artifacts are available in the cited repository.

source_observation.claim: Similar hyperparameter loss-landscape topography was observed across models, datasets, and fidelity levels.

interpretation.claim: Some HPO-relevant landscape properties may generalize across otherwise different modeling scenarios.

application.claim: Compare landscape structure across models, datasets, and fidelities when studying or designing HPO methods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported similarity holds outside the studied models, datasets, fidelities, or configurations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 6 models, 63 datasets, or fidelity levels.
The abstract does not identify the dedicated FLA metrics or fine-grained visualizations.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or independent verification of the reported observations.
